title: Claim Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Measured Versus Designed Claims
Evidence
Reporting Prediction Quality
Learning Record Store
description: A p5.js drag-and-drop sorter in which learners classify ten sentences about the xAPI stream and the Learning Record Store as measured, designed or hoped for, with explanations for correct placements and hints naming the evidence a measured claim would need.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Labeling claims as measured, designed or hoped for
learningObjectives: Classify statements about the xAPI stream as measured, designed or hoped for, and justify the classification by pointing to the evidence that would be required.
prerequisites: Built, designed and hoped-for status tables in Chapters 18 and 20

accessibility.keyboardNotes: Zone buttons place the top card, so the activity can be completed without dragging.
accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: Okabe-Ito zone colors with text labels

controls.label: Top card of the stack (drag onto a zone)
Click a placed chip to review its explanation

assumptions: Card labels follow the book's status statements as of the LRS repository TODO.md dated 2026-09-26.
Results computed on the synthetic cohort count as measured, but about a simulation.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify, then justify by naming the required evidence
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Sorting into category zones with immediate feedback
keyQuestions: Was this observed, and could someone repeat it?
Does the sentence describe a plan or specification rather than a result?
What evidence would turn a hoped-for claim into a measured one?
commonMisconceptions: A precise number is always a measured claim about real learners.
A detailed design means the system is built and working.
A result about a simulation is evidence about real learners.
assessmentOpportunities: First-try accuracy across the ten cards.
Written evidence requirements for hoped-for cards.
